title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative High-Impact Programme for Violence Elimination by 2030 (HIVE Programme).

description.narrative: Contract related to: Spotlight Initiative High-Impact Programme for Violence Elimination by 2030 (HIVE Programme). - Gender equality is a core value and objective of the EU. Over the last few years, there have been important setbacks for gender equality and the enjoyment of human rights by women and girls. Global normative frameworks and international commitments on gender equality have been increasingly questioned, not least sexual and reproductive health and rights. Gender Based Violence (GBV) including Violence Against Women and Girls (VAW/G)[1] has been exacerbated by COVID 19 and is globally on the rise.  With its Gender Action Plan III 2021-2025, the EU reinforces its ambitious engagement for a gender equal world at global, regional and country level. The fight for the elimination of gender based violence continues to be one of the EU priorities, while promoting the equal participation of women and girls in the public sphere. Strong partnerships with civil society, enhanced voice and capacity of women¿s organisations are at the core of GAP III through enhanced dialogue and support at all levels. Through this action, the EU intends to promote its interests and values at global level and more specifically positioned itself on the eradication of gender based violence (GBV), by building and reinforcing coalitions with partners in line with the Generation Equality¿s commitments. The action will build on the EU-UN Spotlight Initiative theory of change and capitalize on its results and lessons learned in 26 countries while ensuring its sustainability. The action pursues two main outcomes : i) strengthen and disseminate knowledge and best practices, expertise, data and research on how to reduce/eliminate GBV expanding and building the sustainability of the Spotlight Initiative; ii) increase global advocacy by civil society and more particularly women¿s rights organisations (WROs), strengthen their capacity and resilience, boosting coalition building and networking.[1] For the purpose of this AD the two terms are used interchangeably, it is understood that GBV is characterised by a broader scope : while women and girls suffer disproportionately from GBV, men and boys can also be targeted. The term is also sometimes used to describe targeted violence against LGBTQI+ populations, when referencing violence related to norms of masculinity/femininity and/or gender norms.
